## Detailed Findings

#### 1. Cline #13422: Hook spawn cwd validation — prevent spawn failures from crashing core process (HIGH ~6h)

- **What**: Cline prevented hook spawn failures from crashing the entire cline-core process. A hook child-process spawn failure emitted "error" on HookProcess with no listener registered, which Node's EventEmitter turns into an uncaught exception — killing the entire core process instead of failing the one hook. Guard: check listenerCount before emit so the rejection (which StdioHookRunner handles) is the only propagation path. Trigger was a workspace root that no longer exists on disk passed as the spawn cwd: Node reports a nonexistent cwd as a misleading ENOENT on the launcher binary ("spawn /bin/sh ENOENT"). Validate cwd existence in HookProcess right before spawning, falling back to no explicit cwd with a warning that names the missing directory. Updated approach: fail hooks with a missing working directory instead of relocating them. Running a hook whose assigned cwd no longer exists from the host process's own working directory would let its relative paths read and write an unrelated location (e.g. the IDE install directory). Reject before spawning, with an error naming the missing directory; the runner reports the hook as failed and the task continues. Also carry pre-spawn failure messages into HookExecutionError details so the cause is not reduced to a bare "exited with code 1".
- **Why**: Hook spawn failure should fail the hook, not crash the entire orchestrator process. Nonexistent cwd should reject with descriptive error, not relocate to process.cwd() and let hook read/write wrong location.
- **Source**: https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/13422 (fix(vscode): prevent hook spawn failures from crashing the core process)
- **Category**: tool (hooks / spawn)
- **Size**: HIGH (~6h — Alexi hooks (src/hooks/) spawn child processes for hook execution. hookExecutor.ts L1-multiple lines likely uses Node.js spawn with cwd option. Implementing same guards: (1) validate cwd exists before spawn (fs.existsSync on cwd path, reject with descriptive error if missing), (2) guard "error" event emit behind listenerCount check so rejection is only propagation path (check emitter.listenerCount('error') > 0 before emit('error', err)), (3) fail with descriptive error instead of relocating to process.cwd() (no fallback cwd, descriptive rejection names missing directory), (4) carry pre-spawn failure details into hook execution error (wrap spawn error with context: hook name, missing cwd path, original error message). Security fix — hook running from wrong cwd is dangerous. Check src/hooks/hookExecutor.ts for spawn logic and add guards).

#### 2. Cline #13680: Langfuse tracer detection minify survivability — structural checks instead of constructor names (MODERATE ~4h)

- **What**: Cline fixed Langfuse telemetry initialization to survive minified release builds. Release binaries are compiled with minify enabled, which renames classes, so initializeLangfuseTelemetry's constructor-name guard never matched "ProxyTracerProvider" and silently returned readiness=false in every production build (hub log: "creating span processor" followed by "initialized readiness=false" with no branch message in between). Dev runs execute unminified source, so same env vars worked there. Replace every constructor-name comparison with checks that survive minification: detect the proxy structurally via getDelegate, distinguish a recording provider from the no-op fallback by its lifecycle methods, and confirm NodeTracerProvider registration by object identity. When a foreign provider already owns the global slot, attach the Langfuse span processor to it when it accepts processors, and otherwise shut down the orphaned provider and report the rejection instead of bailing silently. Verified by bundling the module with Bun minify:true against the real OpenTelemetry packages: previous code reproduces readiness=false (provider class name mangles to "H2"), new code initializes with readiness=true.
- **Why**: Telemetry initialization should survive minified production builds. Constructor-name checks break when minifier renames classes.
- **Source**: https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/13680 (fix(llms): make Langfuse tracer detection survive minified release builds)
- **Category**: tool (telemetry / minify)
- **Size**: MODERATE (~4h — Alexi has NO Langfuse integration currently (no Langfuse imports in src/). Pattern is relevant for ANY telemetry integration using constructor-name checks. Minification renames classes, so `instanceof ClassName` works but `obj.constructor.name === 'ClassName'` fails. If Alexi adds Langfuse (or OpenTelemetry, Sentry, Datadog, any telemetry with class-based initialization), use structural checks instead: (1) detect proxy via getDelegate method existence (`typeof provider.getDelegate === 'function'`), (2) distinguish recording provider from no-op by lifecycle methods (`typeof provider.shutdown === 'function'`), (3) confirm registration by object identity (`trace.getTracerProvider() === myProvider`), (4) when foreign provider owns global slot, attach processor if it accepts them (`typeof provider.addSpanProcessor === 'function'`). Defensive pattern for minified builds. Defer until Langfuse integration is prioritized, but remember pattern for any telemetry integration).

#### 4. Kilocode #13364: Fork runner fallback — GitHub-hosted runners in forks (MODERATE ~2h)

- **What**: Kilocode CI workflows now fall back to GitHub-hosted runners in forks. Blacksmith runners are scoped to the Kilo-Org organization, so every job pinned to blacksmith-* labels queues indefinitely in a fork and is eventually cancelled without running — core test CI is dead in forks, contributors cannot validate a change before opening a PR. Select the runner from github.repository instead of hardcoding it, so the canonical repo keeps its Blacksmith runners byte-for-byte and forks fall back to the GitHub-hosted equivalent. The test.yml unit matrix bakes hosts into JSON, so it routes through emit_settings, which substitutes the two labels from LINUX_HOST/WINDOWS_HOST. pull_request runs execute in the base repo, so PRs sent to Kilo-Org are unaffected; only pushes and PRs inside a fork change behavior. test.yml dropped from fallback because Linux sandbox suite cannot pass on GitHub-hosted runner (Ubuntu 24.04 ships kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1, blocks Bubblewrap user-namespace bootstrap, test asserts support.available is true unconditionally on Linux).
- **Why**: Fork contributors should be able to run CI tests before opening a PR. Hardcoded custom runner labels queue forever in forks.
- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/13364 (ci: fall back to GitHub-hosted runners in forks)
- **Category**: ci (GitHub Actions / fork-friendly)
- **Size**: MODERATE (~2h — Alexi CI workflows (.github/workflows/agent*.yml, auto-implement.yml, ci-auto-fix.yml, ci.yml, test.yml, lint.yml, format.yml) use GitHub-hosted runners (runs-on: ubuntu-latest, windows-latest). No custom runners, no Blacksmith labels. Pattern is fork-friendly CI: detect fork via `github.repository != 'Kilo-Org/kilocode'`, substitute runner labels. Alexi is already fork-friendly (GitHub-hosted runners work in forks), but if Alexi switches to custom runners (self-hosted, Blacksmith, larger machines), implement same fallback pattern: (1) add workflow env vars LINUX_HOST/WINDOWS_HOST with ternary `github.repository == 'owner/repo' ? 'custom-label' : 'ubuntu-latest'`, (2) use env var in runs-on. Pattern is defensive CI hygiene. SKIP for now since Alexi uses GitHub-hosted runners).

#### 8. Cline #13562: History cost estimate suppression for subscription-billed tasks (LOW ~3h)

- **What**: Cline hides history cost estimates for subscription-billed tasks. Task-header fix for subscription providers could not reach history: history rows render the stored totalCost (an API-rate estimate) and do not know which provider ran the task, so the history page printed $X.XXXX on every row and the recent-task chips in an empty chat view rendered a $ chip even for subscription-billed tasks. SDK session records already persist the provider (CLI's history view uses it), but VS Code mappers dropped it. Map it through both transports (HistoryItem.apiProvider for state-pushed taskHistory, TaskItem.api_provider for getTaskHistory) and suppress the dollar figure per row when that provider's usageCostDisplay is not "show", via a new useUsageCostVisibility predicate shared by both surfaces. Rows without a recorded provider (tasks predating the field, legacy imports) keep showing the stored value.
- **Why**: Subscription-billed tasks (OpenAI Codex, Claude subscription) should not show cost estimates in history. Cost estimate is per-token API rate, meaningless for subscription users.
- **Source**: https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/13562 (fix: hide history cost estimates for subscription-billed tasks)
- **Category**: cli (UI / cost display)
- **Size**: LOW (~3h — Alexi CLI history view (src/cli/commands/sessions.ts listSessions L1-multiple lines, src/cli/tui/history.tsx if TUI history exists) shows cost tracking via src/core/costTracker.ts. Check if Alexi supports multiple provider billing models (usage vs subscription). src/providers/modelCatalog.ts defines models, check if usageCostDisplay or billing model field exists. If Alexi supports subscription providers (e.g. ChatGPT Plus via API, Claude Pro), hide cost in history for those sessions. Pattern: (1) persist provider id in session record (sessionManager.ts already persists model, check if provider persisted), (2) load provider billing model (modelCatalog.ts or routing-config.json), (3) suppress cost display when billing model is subscription. Small feature if billing models differentiated. Check billing.ts and costTracker.ts for existing cost logic. Defer unless multiple billing models exist).
